title: Measurement accuracy, S parameters, VNAs
blurb: Explain what limits meter and counter accuracy, read S parameters, calibrate a VNA, find Q, and test SSB for intermodulation.

E4B01.why: A counter counts cycles over a gate set by its oscillator, so **time base accuracy** limits it.
E4B01.trap: Attenuators and dividers don't set how long it counts.

E4B02.why: **Full-scale volts × ohms per volt** = input impedance. A 10 V range at 20 kΩ/V is 200 kΩ.
E4B02.trap: Ohms per volt describes loading, not power drawn or shunt size.

E4B03.why: **S21** is signal in at port 1, measured at port 2: **forward gain**.

E4B04.why: **S11**: in and measured at port 1, so input reflection (**return loss**, equivalent to VSWR).
E4B04.trap: S22 is the same idea at the output port.

E4B05.why: VNA calibration uses three known loads: **short, open and 50 Ω**.
E4B05.trap: A resonant circuit isn't a fixed reference, and 75 Ω and 90 Ω aren't the standard calibration loads.

E4B06.trap: Adding them (125 W) treats reflected power as if the load absorbed it.

E4B07.why: The subscripts name the **ports** where the measurement is made.
E4B07.trap: They are port numbers, not time or data quality.

E4B08.why: **Q = centre frequency ÷ bandwidth**, so the bandwidth of the frequency response gives Q.
E4B08.trap: Resonant frequency alone doesn't give Q; you also need the bandwidth.

E4B09.why: A two-port VNA measures how a device responds across frequency: **filter frequency response**.
E4B09.trap: Phase noise, rise time and forward power need other instruments.

E4B10.why: IMD needs **two AF tones, not harmonically related**, in. A **spectrum analyzer** on the RF out shows the products.
E4B10.trap: The tones go in at audio, not RF, and a logic analyzer can't show RF spectrum.

E4B11.why: A VNA measures input impedance, output impedance and reflection coefficient: **all of them**.
